clue.text: Soft stage effect shows promise

definitions.note: a noun: a plighting is a pledge, the act of giving one's word

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
lighting is an effect used on a theatre stage

explanation.surface: A gently lit scene in a play turns out to be full of promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To plight one's troth is to pledge it, so a plighting is a solemn pledge given.

clue.text: Crucial point as quartet comes in to play snooker

indicators.note: comes in to says the quartet's letters are put inside the snooker word

parts.note: to pot is to sink a ball in snooker
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: At the key moment, a group of four arrives for a snooker game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the central point on which something turns, hence a crucial or decisive point.

clue.text: Bill's singing well

definitions.meaning: a bill is a statement of money owed
a singer on good form is said to be in good voice

explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill for goods; split as two words, it describes a singer in fine form.

clue.text: Metallic noise initially confused Dutch radio station

indicators.note: only the first letters of the two words are mixed up, swapping places between them

parts.note: silver is a metal, used here as a descriptive word
a hum is a low continuous noise

explanation.surface: A tinny sound at first baffles listeners of a Dutch broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially confused' swaps the first letters of SILVER and HUM, giving HILVER SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilversum is the Dutch town that is home to the Netherlands' broadcasting, long printed on radio dials.

clue.text: Problem, non-religious, recurring in Hibernian writer

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the Irish word

parts.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish

indicators.note: recurring is read as running back, so the shortened problem word is turned round
non- says the religious person, in crosswords a nun, is taken out of the problem word

parts.note: a conundrum is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: An Irish author keeps returning to a secular difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' is a noun here: a member of a religious order, a nun. 'Hibernian' looks like the football club but just means Irish; 'recurring' reads as running backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch was a Dublin-born novelist and philosopher, so she is a writer and, by birth, Hibernian.

clue.text: Encountering no resistance, seize rabbit

indicators.note: meeting no resistance means the resistance letter is dropped from the seize word

parts.note: to grab is to seize
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Meeting no opposition, someone grabs a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is British slang for chatter, to rabbit on, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit is to talk on and on, which is the same as idle chatter or gab.

clue.text: With drink, a new driver's going to : kill someone

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits
L is the learner plate on a new driver's car in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone driving on L-plates after a drink is a danger to others.
explanation.walkthrough: An L-plate marks a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To total, in informal use, is to wreck completely, extended to killing someone.

clue.text: Old poet's day is over — who cares?

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the day abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday
so? is a dismissive way of saying who cares

explanation.surface: An elderly poet's time has passed, and nobody minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' turns SAT back to TAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was a sixteenth-century Italian poet, author of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Travel to endlessly foul-smelling port

parts.note: a trip is a journey, travel

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the smelly word is cut

parts.note: olid is a rare word for stinking

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a port that smells endlessly bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is a Mediterranean port, the capital of Libya; there is also a port of that name in Lebanon.

clue.text: Crikey! My road to be demolished official!

parts.note: lor is a dialect exclamation of surprise, like crikey

indicators.note: demolishing knocks a thing down, so the letters of my road are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone is outraged to learn their road will be pulled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be demolished' rearranges MY ROAD into DMAYOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lord Mayor is the civic head of a large British city, an official post.

clue.text: Composer slammed lid after examination

indicators.note: after says the scrambled lid follows the examination word

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination

indicators.note: slammed is read as violently treated, so the letters of lid are knocked about

explanation.surface: A musician bangs down a piano lid after a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was a Venetian Baroque composer, best known for The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Transport row gets top coverage

parts.note: a bus is a form of transport
a tier is a row, one of a series rising above another

explanation.surface: A dispute about public transport makes the front page.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustier is a close-fitting strapless top, so it covers the upper body.

clue.text: Husband leaves several times, just for a moment

indicators.note: leaves says the husband letter goes out of the several-times word

parts.note: thrice means three times

explanation.surface: A husband walks out repeatedly, though only briefly each time.
explanation.definitionFit: A trice is a very brief moment, as in the phrase in a trice.

clue.text: Comic's ROM exchanged for a smaller system

indicators.note: exchanged means the letters swap places among themselves

parts.note: the comic word with its s kept as a letter
read-only memory, taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian's computer memory is swapped for a smaller unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' rearranges COMICS and ROM; here the s of Comic's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A microcosm is a world in miniature, a small system mirroring a larger one.

clue.text: It's night: called out for illumination

indicators.note: out is read as wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Night has fallen, and someone calls for the lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NIGHT and CALLED; 'It's' joins the fodder to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlelight is the light given by candles, a form of illumination.

clue.text: Outstanding freshness, I say!

indicators.note: I say signals the word is spoken, its sound giving the answer

parts.note: dew is used figuratively for freshness, as in the dew of youth

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a remarkable freshness.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is due is still unpaid, which is what outstanding means of a bill.

clue.text: Dialled panel to reveal bribe by directors

parts.note: dash is a West African word for a bribe or tip
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: A control panel exposes a backhander taken by company bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's dashboard is the panel of dials and gauges in front of the driver.

clue.text: Lucky chance to have a bathe in peace

indicators.note: in places the bathe word inside the peace word

parts.note: serenity is calm, peace
a dip is a quick bathe

explanation.surface: It is a stroke of luck to have a quiet swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is the happy knack of finding good things by accident, a fortunate chance.

clue.text: Irish girl and boy were troublesome

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An Irish girl and boy caused bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that irritated were annoying, causing trouble or discomfort.

clue.text: Heavy vehicle turning West runs into pedestrian

indicators.note: runs into puts the turned name inside the pedestrian word

parts.note: a stroller is someone walking at leisure

indicators.note: turning means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Mae West, the American film actress

explanation.surface: A truck swings west and hits someone on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction; it is the actress Mae West, whose first name 'turning' makes EAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamroller is a heavy road vehicle with large rollers for flattening surfaces.

clue.text: So absorbed by English (Tyneside) rave

indicators.note: absorbed by puts the so word inside the letters that follow

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
thus means so, therefore

explanation.surface: Tyneside folk get carried away about the English.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to speak with great enthusiasm, to rave about something.

clue.text: Old police force rejected disreputable type

indicators.note: rejected is read as thrown back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: the RUC, the Royal Ulster Constabulary, was Northern Ireland's police until 2001

explanation.surface: A former police force turned away a shady character.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel dog and, by extension, a contemptible person.

clue.text: Very likely animal to mount a tree?

parts.note: the beast most likely to be found climbing a tree is a feline, the pet that gets stuck up one
an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: Which creature is most likely to climb a tree?
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as one; the cat, mountain and A are three pieces, with 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The catalpa is a North American and Asian tree with large leaves and long bean-like pods.

clue.text: Result of 1 ac —- both later spliced

indicators.note: spliced means joined together, here mixing the two words into one set of letters

explanation.surface: Two people who make a promise both get married later.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac is 1 across, PLIGHTING; 'spliced', British slang for married, rearranges BOTH and LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plighting of troth leads to a betrothal, an engagement to marry.

clue.text: Lights in Irish county snapped off

indicators.note: snapped off means the end is broken away, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Offaly is a county in the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: The lamps in an Irish county were switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights are the lungs of slaughtered animals, a kind of offal.

clue.text: Flyer taking the French championship

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a flyer
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An aviator wins a French title.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a championship, as when a boxer holds a title.

clue.text: Nigel's lost his marbles in Scottish town

indicators.note: losing one's marbles is going mad, so the letters of the name go wild

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Nigel has gone mad in a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost his marbles' rearranges NIGEL, nodding to the Elgin Marbles taken from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a town in Moray, in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: A lock closed early with some hesitation — it'll hold water

indicators.note: closed early means stopped before the end, so the hair word loses its last letter

parts.note: a quiff is a lock of hair brushed up at the front
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone haltingly explains that a lock was shut before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door; it is hair, QUIFF, and 'closed early' cuts its last F.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquifer is underground rock that holds and yields water.

clue.text: Naked, in this nasty cold sort of weather?

definitions.text: Naked, in this nasty cold sort of weather?

parts.words: Naked, in this nasty cold sort of weather?
parts.note: to be naked is to be in the buff, and bitter, damp chilly weather is described with the same short word

explanation.definitionFit: Raw means bitterly cold and damp of weather, and 'in the raw' means naked.

clue.text: Some eating at elegant table

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people are dining at a smart table.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateleg table has hinged legs that swing out like gates to support drop leaves.

clue.text: Live comfortably with daughter

indicators.note: with says the daughter letter is set alongside the comfort word, here in front

parts.note: to live well is to live comfortably

explanation.surface: Someone lives in comfort with their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live there.

clue.text: Shy and tense

parts.note: with means along with, and
drawn means strained, tense

explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawn person is reserved and retiring, that is, shy.
